correctness.rationale: All parameter boundaries are covered: three nonnegative cyclic zero gaps, including zeros, equality patterns and the all-ones degenerate periodic word. The binary periodic counting identity is proved by summing two-sided extension deficits and telescoping factor complexity. The complete bispecial classification follows from the three predecessor/successor gap contexts, repeated inner-gap cases, and uniqueness of two consecutive gaps unless all three agree. Counting gives the the maximum-gap/distinct-gap formula; simple sum constraints prove fixed-length extrema. The standalone program independently verifies the exact factor sets for all 1000 ordered triples in \(\{0,\ldots,9\}^3\) and the stated extremal classification for \(n=3,\ldots,33\), without treating bounded checking as a proof.

value.rationale: Circular minimal absent words are a standard alignment-free sequence invariant, and weight three is the first cyclic marker class with up to three distinct inter-marker gaps. The theorem gives an exact infinite-family classification by only the longest gap and equality type, not isolated enumerations or a simple substitution. It supplies a new complete bispecial-factor classification and sharp minimum, maximum, and all maximizing gap multisets at every length; these explain precise antidictionary complexity in sparse-marker cycles. The result does not claim broader sequence-reconstruction consequences or independent certification.
